title: Block: Best So Far With an Index
oneLiner: Walk an array with its index and return the position of the largest value (the first one on a tie).
keyTakeaway: Start the best so far at the first element, never at 0: an array of negatives has no 0 in it.
explanation:
Return the index of the largest value in nums, the first such index when it repeats, or -1 for an empty array.

The construct is a loop that sees both the index and the value (a for loop with i in C#, enumerate in Python) plus one "best so far" variable. Seeding the best with element 0 instead of a made-up number is the habit to build.

starterCode.python:
def index_of_max(nums):
    # 1. Return -1 straight away if the array is empty.
    # 2. Start the best index at 0, so the first element is the best so far.
    # 3. Walk the rest of the array with its index.
    # 4. When a value is strictly greater than the best so far, remember its index.
    # 5. Return the best index.
    return -1

gotchas: Starting the best value at 0, which is wrong when every value is negative.
Using >= instead of >, which returns the last index on a tie.
